nodes.label: Inline #[cfg(test)] test convention
nodes.rationale: Tests live at the bottom of the source file they cover; a file under tests/ is added only when a test genuinely cannot see what it needs from inside the crate.

nodes.label: File tool path jail (fs_tools::resolve)
nodes.rationale: .. is normalised lexically before the prefix check because starts_with is component-wise, and symlinks are canonicalised. run_bash is deliberately NOT confined — jailing a shell needs a real sandbox.

nodes.label: Staging directory for mutating file tools
nodes.rationale: A crash-safety mechanism, NOT a security boundary: it sanitises its own mirror then copies to the unsanitised target. The path jail is the boundary.

nodes.label: Three tool-registration entry points
nodes.rationale: try_register fails on a name collision (untrusted MCP tools), register panics (trusted startup wiring), replace overwrites deliberately (upgrading keyless web_search once an Exa key exists).

nodes.label: mcp__{server}__{tool} namespacing
nodes.rationale: Without the prefix a remote server publishing read_file would displace the sandboxed built-in; the wire call still uses the bare remote name.

nodes.label: tool_defs() sorted by name for prefix caching
nodes.rationale: The tool array is part of the prefix providers cache on; a HashMap's order would miss the cache on every request with no visible symptom.

nodes.label: Every tool_use answered by a tool_result
nodes.rationale: agent.rs seeds the results vector and fills it in rather than appending, so the invariant cannot regress even on cancellation. A dangling tool_use makes the next request fail outright.

nodes.label: API key redaction choke point
nodes.rationale: One choke point in run_one_tool covers the transcript, the session database and the next provider request together.

nodes.label: AgentEvent adjacently-tagged serialization
nodes.rationale: It IS the --output-format stream-json wire format, so variant and field names are a public interface; app.rs matches exhaustively with no wildcard, so a new variant always needs a TUI arm too.

nodes.label: smith-core testkit / ScriptedProvider
nodes.rationale: Running past the end of a script panics on purpose — a turn making more requests than scripted is a finding, not something to paper over with a default reply.

nodes.label: MSRV 1.88
nodes.rationale: The floor comes from the dependency graph (ratatui 0.30, darling 0.24), not from first-party syntax.

nodes.label: Env API keys outrank saved config
